sum: A three-week route in Nepal's far east: up the Ghunsa valley to Pangpema below Kanchenjunga's north face, across the Sele La and Mirgin La, then to Oktang on the south side.

guide.note: This is a restricted area: the permit is issued only through a registered trekking agency and you must be accompanied by a licensed guide, whether you come alone or in a group. A guide who knows the route also matters on the long pass day between the Sele La and Cheram, where the trail is faint in snow or cloud and there is no shelter.

access: Fly from Kathmandu to Bhadrapur in the south-eastern Terai, then drive north through the tea country of Ilam to Taplejung, usually over two days. From Taplejung a rough jeep track follows the Tamor river to Sekathum. Coming out, jeeps meet groups at Yamphudin when the track is open.

photo.a: The ice-hung north face of Kanchenjunga rises above the broad, snow-covered Kanchenjunga glacier, with dark moraine rubble in the foreground.

includes: lodge beds; meals in most packages but not all
flights to Bhadrapur and the jeep to Taplejung in some packages (confirm)

permits.name: Kanchenjunga restricted area permit
permits.fee: USD 20 per person per week for the first four weeks, then USD 25 a week

fees.per: person per week for the first four weeks, then USD 25 a week

permits.where: Department of Immigration in Kathmandu, through a registered trekking agency only.

permits.name: Kanchenjunga Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, normally arranged by your agency with the restricted-area permit. Foreign trekkers are also registered at check posts on the trail, for example at Ghunsa.

transportText: Flights between Kathmandu and Bhadrapur both ways, and a jeep seat between Bhadrapur and Taplejung each way
transportExtra: local jeeps between Taplejung and the trailheads
tips: Bring all the cash you need in rupees from Kathmandu, Birtamod or Taplejung; there is nowhere to withdraw money after that.
A warm sleeping bag is essential. Lodges above Ghunsa give you a bed and, at best, a blanket.
Carry water treatment and a spare way to charge a phone and headlamp. Solar charging at the high lodges is limited and costs extra.
Before leaving Ghunsa and Cheram, have your guide confirm which huts at Lhonak, the Sele La and Ramche are open, particularly early and late in the season.
Count the days on your restricted-area permit carefully. It is charged by the week, and a weather delay can push you into the next one.

days.t: Fly to Bhadrapur, drive to Ilam
days.note: A 45-minute flight to the Terai, then three to four hours by road up through tea estates to Ilam. Some groups push on towards Taplejung the same day, which makes for a very long drive.
A slow, winding hill road by way of Phidim. Taplejung is the last town with banks, cash machines and a proper bazaar, so finish your shopping and withdraw what you need here.
A rough track along the Tamor river through Mitlung, Chiruwa and Tapethok, with permit checks on the way. If landslides have blocked it, expect to walk part of the distance and lose a day.
Up the narrow Ghunsa Khola gorge on a trail that crosses the river several times, then climbs steeply to a few houses on a shelf far above it. Hot, humid and harder than the map suggests.
A day in dense forest of bamboo, oak and rhododendron, with waterfalls across the valley and a steep final pull to Gyabla. The path is narrow and slippery after rain.

The valley widens and the air turns cooler. You pass the Tibetan settlement of Phale with its small monastery, then walk through larch and juniper to Ghunsa, where the police post checks permits again.
Climb a few hundred metres up the hillside above the village in the morning and come back down for lunch. This is also the last good place to wash, charge batteries and buy snacks.

North along the river through forest, then across an exposed landslide slope where you move one at a time and do not stop. Jannu's north face comes into view shortly before the stone houses of Kambachen.
Walk up the side valley towards the Jannu Glacier for a closer look at the north face, going only as high as feels comfortable, then return to sleep at the same height.

A gradual climb over boulder fields and old moraine beside the Kanchenjunga Glacier, with stretches beneath loose slopes where stones come down. Lhonak is a windy, sandy flat with a few basic huts, and the night is cold.
why: Sleeping altitude rises 680 m, well over the 500 m guideline even with a rest night next to it.

days.t: Pangpema, the north base camp, and back to Lhonak
days.note: Leave early and follow the edge of the moraine, which has slumped in places, to the hut at Pangpema. The north face fills the head of the valley. Most people return to Lhonak for a better night's sleep.
A long descent that retraces two upward days in one. Going down is quick, but give the landslide slope below Kambachen the same care as on the way up.

days.t: Ghunsa to the Sele La huts
days.note: A steep climb out of the valley through rhododendron and juniper to open ridges, then a traverse to the huts near the Sele La. There is little water on the way, so fill your bottles before you leave.
why: Sleeping altitude rises 815 m in one day, well over the 500 m guideline. Split the climb if you can.

days.t: Over Sinion La, Mirgin La and Sinelapche La to Cheram
days.note: The hardest day: three passes in a row over rough, exposed ground with no lodge between them, then a steep drop of nearly 800 m to Cheram. Start at first light. Published heights for these passes differ by up to 200 m.

days.t: Cheram to Ramche and the Oktang viewpoint
days.note: Follow the valley beside the Yalung Glacier to the meadow at Ramche, leave your bag and continue to the chorten at Oktang for the south side of the mountain. If cloud has already come in, go at first light tomorrow instead.
why: Sleeping altitude rises 710 m, well over the 500 m guideline even with a rest night next to it.

days.note: Back past Cheram and on down the Simbuwa Khola into tall forest of fir and rhododendron. A big loss of height and an easy day for the lungs, though the trail is rooty and wet in places.

days.t: Tortong to Yamphudin over Lasiya Bhanjyang
days.note: A stiff forest climb to the ridge, skirting a very large landslide that has eaten into the old path; cross the affected stretch quickly. Then a long descent to the fields of Yamphudin, the first real village since Ghunsa.

n: 1st Kanchenjunga South Base Camp hotel and lodge

days.note: A rough track leads out to the main road south. When it is cut you walk on for five or six hours to Khebang, or further, to meet the vehicle, which is one reason to keep a spare day in hand.

days.t: Drive to Bhadrapur, fly to Kathmandu
days.note: Three to four hours down to the plains for an afternoon flight. Bhadrapur is far more dependable than the mountain airstrips, but the road can be slow, so do not book the earliest departure.
